words.gram: m. gen. sg. caus. pres. part. √gras

hindi: ब्राह्मण को अपेय अथवा अभक्ष्य निगलवाने वाले को सर्वोच्च दण्ड; क्षत्रिय को मध्यम; वैश्य को प्रथम साहस-दण्ड; शूद्र को चौवन पण का दण्ड।
english: For one who makes a Brahmin swallow what is undrinkable or inedible, the highest fine; [for doing so to] a Kshatriya, the middle [fine]; a Vaishya, the first fine for rashness; a Shudra, a fine of fifty-four paṇas.
notes: Elliptical: the offence is understood for each varṇa and the nouns daṇḍa/sāhasa are carried over (bracketed in English only). uttama/madhyama/pūrva are the three grades of the fine for rashness (sāhasa-daṇḍa); amounts are not stated here. catuṣ.pañcāśat = catuḥ-pañcāśat 'four-and-fifty' = 54.

hindi: स्वयं निगलने वालों को देश से रहित कर देना चाहिए।
english: Those who swallow [it] themselves are to be made landless (without a territory).
notes: Object of grasitāraḥ is not stated (continues from unit 1). nirviṣaya, literally 'without territory (viṣaya)', is usually understood as banished from the realm; kept literal.

hindi: दूसरे के घर जाने पर दिन में प्रथम साहस-दण्ड, रात में मध्यम।
english: On going to another's house, by day the first fine for rashness, by night the middle [fine].
notes: abhigamana is literally 'going up to'; unit 4 uses praviśataḥ for entering. In 'madhyamaḥ' the sāhasa-daṇḍa is understood.

hindi: दिन अथवा रात में शस्त्र सहित प्रवेश करने वाले को सर्वोच्च दण्ड।
english: For one who enters armed, by day or by night, the highest fine.
notes: What is entered is not stated (continues from unit 3).

hindi: भिक्षुक और वैदेहक, मतवाला और पागल, बल से, आपत्ति में, अत्यन्त निकट रहने वाले और जिनका प्रवेश प्रचलित है, ये दण्ड के अयोग्य हैं; निषेध को छोड़कर।
english: A mendicant and a trader (vaidehaka), a drunk and a mad person, [those acting] by force, in distress, those very close, and those whose entry is established are not to be fined, except [where there is] a prohibition.
notes: Obscure: 'balād āpadi' (by force / in distress) is taken as two items of the list; whether it describes the entrant is not stated. pravṛtta-praveśa is kept literal ('whose entry is established/under way'); the sense (e.g. those who enter in the course of regular business) is uncertain. atisannikṛṣṭa = 'very near' (neighbours is a possible sense). vaidehaka = trader per GLOSSARY. anyatra pratiṣedhāt = 'except from prohibition'.

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. ā-√ruh

words.gloss: of one who breaks village, garden, enclosure

hindi: अपने घर की चहारदीवारी पर आधी रात के बाद चढ़ने वाले को प्रथम साहस-दण्ड; दूसरे के घर की चहारदीवारी पर चढ़ने वाले को मध्यम; और गाँव, उद्यान या बाड़ को तोड़ने वाले को।
english: For one who climbs over the enclosure of his own house after midnight, the first fine for rashness; [for one who climbs over the enclosure] of another's house, the middle [fine]; and [for one] who breaks into a village, garden or fence.
notes: virātra is taken as 'dead of night, midnight' (alternative: after the night is over); the fine for the last clause is not stated (the last ca-clause leaves it open; the middle fine is likely but not said). parivāra = enclosure/wall (alternative sense 'retinue' unlikely with ārohataḥ). bhedin: gen. sg. 'of one breaking'; 'breaks into' is a natural reading of bheda. ārāma = garden, vāṭa = fence/enclosure.

hindi: जिनकी बहुमूल्य वस्तुएँ ज्ञात हों, ऐसे सार्थिक गाँवों के भीतर ठहरें।
english: Caravan-members, with their valuables known, should stay within the villages.
notes: sāra = valuables (GLOSSARY 12.1); jñāta-sāra literally 'whose valuables are known'; by whom is not stated.

words.gram: n. acc. sg. pp. caus. pra-√vas

hindi: इनका चुराया और दूर भेजा हुआ, जो बाहर नहीं गया, रात में ग्राम-स्वामी दे।
english: The village lord should give [for] what of these is robbed and made to go away, not gone out, at night.
notes: Obscure syntax. dadyāt 'should give' is read as 'make good' (compensation) from context, and 'give [for]' is bracketed. pravāsita of goods: literally 'caused to go abroad/away' (GLOSSARY has 'done away with' for persons only). anirgata could qualify the goods or refer to the caravan-members not having left; not settled.

words.gram: n. acc. sg. pp. caus. pra-√vas

hindi: अथवा गाँवों के बीच के क्षेत्रों में चुराए हुए और दूर भेजे हुए को चरागाहों का अध्यक्ष दे।
english: Or, [for] what is robbed or made to go away in the intervals between villages, the superintendent of pastures should give.
notes: As in unit 8, 'give' is read as making good; the object is bracketed. vivīta = pasture (GLOSSARY 8.4). grāma-antara can also mean 'other villages'; 'intervals between villages' chosen.

hindi: जो चरागाह नहीं हैं उनका चोर-रज्जुक।
english: Of the non-pasture [tracts] — the cora-rajjuka.
notes: Predicate omitted (dadyāt carried from unit 9 is likely); left open. cora-rajjuka kept untranslated: literally 'thief-rope(-man)'; probably an officer who catches thieves, but the sense is not certain. avivīta = 'not a pasture'; the noun 'tracts' is not in the Sanskrit.

hindi: फिर भी अरक्षितों की खोज सीमा को रोककर करें।
english: Even so, for the unprotected [places] they should make a search by closing off the boundary.
notes: vicayaṃ dadyuḥ is literally 'should give a search' (idiom: conduct one); read as 'make a search'. aguptānām has no noun (places/tracts/persons); 'places' bracketed. avarodha = blocking/closing off; 'by blockade of the boundary' is the same sense. Subject (plural) is not named.

hindi: सीमा-अवरोध न होने पर पाँच गाँवों का समूह अथवा दस गाँवों का समूह।
english: When there is no boundary-blocking, [it is] a group of five villages or a group of ten villages.
notes: Predicate omitted; the group is probably the body responsible, but the text does not say. asīma-avarodha = 'absence of boundary-blocking' (or 'blocking of a non-boundary').

hindi: कमज़ोर घर, बिना टेक की गाड़ी, ऊँचा खम्भा, बिना आश्रय का शस्त्र, अथवा खुला गड्ढा, कुआँ या फन्दे वाला गड्ढा बनाकर हिंसा होने पर शारीरिक चोट समझे।
english: Having made a weak house, an unpropped cart, a raised post, an unsupported weapon, or an uncovered pit, well or trap-fall, in a case of injury one should know [it as] physical injury (daṇḍa-pāruṣya).

text_flags.why: possible: ūrdha is not a word; ūrdhva 'upright, raised' is expected (a post)

notes: Obscure list; which adjective goes with which noun is uncertain (apraticchanna probably governs the pit, well and trap-fall; anuttabdha probably the cart). 'Having made' (kṛtvā) is kept literal: the sense is that setting up such a hazard counts as the offence if injury follows. daṇḍa-pāruṣya = physical injury as in Book 3 (GLOSSARY 8.3 note), not 'harshness of punishment'.

words.gloss: in taking away the reins of a tameable [animal]
in the use of an untamed [one]
in the throwing of wood, clod, stone, stick, arrow, arm
closing particle (end of the quoted call)

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. pra-√kruś

hindi: वृक्ष काटने में, दमन-योग्य की लगाम हटाने में, चौपायों में बिना सधे हुए के उपयोग में अथवा हाँकने में, लकड़ी, ढेला, पत्थर, डण्डा, बाण या बाँह फेंकने में, वाहन में और हाथी से टक्कर में “हट जाओ” चिल्लाने वाला दण्ड के अयोग्य है।
english: In cutting a tree, in taking away the reins of a tameable [animal], in the use of an untamed one among quadrupeds, or in driving, in the throwing of wood, clod, stone, stick, arrow or arm, in a vehicle and in a collision with an elephant, one who cries out “Move away!” is not to be fined.

text_flags.why: possible: daṃya is not a word; damya 'to be tamed' is expected (anusvāra for m)
stray s/m for saṃ: saṃghaṭṭana 'collision' is expected
possible: the r of pra-√kruś has dropped; pra-kruś 'cry out' is expected

notes: Typed-text slips are corrected only in words. The list is obscure: damya-raśmi-haraṇa taken as 'removal of the reins of a tameable (animal)'; catuṣpadānām adānta-sevane vāhane = 'among quadrupeds, in using untamed ones, or in driving' (vāhana could also be 'riding/conveying'). 'yāne hastinā ca saṃghaṭṭane' is ambiguous: 'in a collision, in a vehicle and with an elephant' (as given) or 'in a collision with a vehicle and an elephant'. The quoted call 'apehi' is opened and closed; iti is only the closing particle of the quotation.

hindi: क्रोधित हाथी से मारा गया — द्रोण भर अन्न, मद्य का घड़ा, माला और लेप, दाँत साफ करने की वस्तु और वस्त्र दे।
english: One killed by an enraged elephant — [one] should give a droṇa of food, a jar of liquor, garland and ointment, tooth-cleaning [materials] and a cloth.
notes: The giver and the recipient are not stated, so the unit is left as a dash construction. droṇa is a measure and stays droṇa. mālya-anulepana is taken as garland and ointment (one dvandva); danta-pramārjana is literally 'cleaning of teeth'. The next unit (16) gives a quoted reason.

words.gloss: with the concluding bath of the horse sacrifice

hindi: “हाथी से वध अश्वमेध के अवभृथ-स्नान के समान है” — पैर धोना।
english: “Killing by an elephant is equal to the concluding bath (avabhṛtha) of the horse sacrifice” — the washing of the feet.
notes: Syntax obscure: the quoted statement is followed by 'pāda-prakṣālana' without a verb; it is probably the last item of what is given in unit 15 (or the reason for it), but the text does not say. Kept literal and left open with a dash. iti closes the quotation and is not rendered.

words.gloss: in the killing of an uninvolved person

hindi: तटस्थ के वध में चालक को सर्वोच्च दण्ड।
english: In the killing of an uninvolved person, the highest fine for the driver.
notes: udāsīna here is a bystander (one not involved), not the 'neutral king' of the maṇḍala theory. yātṛ is literally 'goer'; 'driver' is the sense required by unit 25 (bāle yātari). A person is not named in the Sanskrit but is meant (vadha of an udāsīna).

words.gram: m. acc. sg. pres. part. pass. √hiṃs
m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. a-√muc

words.gloss: of one who was cried out to

hindi: सींग वाले अथवा दाढ़ वाले से सताए जा रहे को न छुड़ाने वाले स्वामी को प्रथम साहस-दण्ड; जिसके प्रति पुकार की गई उसका दुगुना।
english: For an owner who does not release [one] being hurt by a horned or fanged [animal], the first fine for rashness; for [one] who has been cried out to, double.
notes: śṛṅgin/daṃṣṭrin = 'having horns / having fangs or tusks'; 'animal' is not in the Sanskrit. hiṃsyamānam has no stated gender. pratikruṣṭasya is literally 'of him who was called/cried out to' (the owner who was asked for help); sense inferred.

words.gloss: by a horned and a fanged [animal]

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. √han

hindi: सींग वाले और दाढ़ वाले से आपस में मरवाने वाले का वह और उतना दण्ड।
english: For one who has a horned and a fanged [animal] kill each other, the fine is that and so much.
notes: Literal: 'that and so much, the fine'. tat is probably the value of the animal killed and tāvat an equal amount; not stated, so kept literal. Same formula in unit 21.

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. √vah
m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. pra-√vas

hindi: देव-पशु, साँड, बैल अथवा कुमारी गाय को वहन कराने वाले को पाँच सौ का दण्ड; दूर भेजने वाले को सर्वोच्च।
english: For one who makes a god's animal, a bull, an ox or a young cow carry [a load], a fine of five hundred; for one who sends [it] away, the highest.
notes: The unit of five hundred (paṇas) is not stated. deva-paśu = animal belonging to a god (dedicated); ṛṣabha 'bull', ukṣan 'ox'. vāhayati = 'makes carry/draw' (use as a beast of burden). pravāsayataḥ is literal 'causes to go away/abroad'; the exception clause in unit 21 (anyatra deva-pitṛ-kāryebhyaḥ) suggests it may mean killing off, but this is not certain (GLOSSARY has 'do away with' only for persons). The noun 'fine' with uttamaḥ is carried over.

words.gloss: of those useful for wool, milk, carrying and breeding
for the tasks of gods and ancestors

hindi: ऊन, दूध, भार ढोने और प्रजनन के लिए उपयोगी छोटे पशुओं को न देने पर वह और उतना दण्ड है, और दूर भेजने पर; देवों और पितरों के कार्यों को छोड़कर।
english: For small animals useful for wool, milk, carrying and breeding: in non-giving, the fine is that and so much, and in sending away; except for the tasks of the gods and ancestors.
notes: adāne ('non-giving') is obscure: what is not given (the animal back, its due) is not stated; ādāna 'taking' is a possible alternative but the printed form is kept. Formula tac ca tāvac ca daṇḍaḥ as in unit 19. pravāsana literal 'sending away' (see unit 20); the exception for rites of gods and ancestors suggests killing.

words.gloss: come athwart or face to face

words.gram: n. nom. sg. pres. part. prati-ā-√sṛ

words.gloss: in a crush of animals and men

hindi: जिसकी नाक की रस्सी कटी हो, जुआ टूटा हो, जो तिरछा या सामने आया हो अथवा पीछे हट रहा हो, पहिये से जुड़ा हो — ऐसे के चालक को, अथवा पशुओं और मनुष्यों की भीड़ में हिंसा होने पर, दण्ड नहीं होना चाहिए।
english: In an injury [caused by a vehicle] with a cut nose-rope, a broken yoke, one come athwart or face to face, or backing up, or fitted with a wheel, or in a crush of animals and men, the driver is not to be fined.
notes: Obscure. The noun ('vehicle') is not in the Sanskrit and is bracketed. nasya = nose-rope of draught animals. tiryak-pratimukha-āgata is taken as 'come athwart or head-on' (one karmadhāraya); pratyāsarat is taken as 'backing up/retreating' (cf. pratyāsāra 'retreat', GLOSSARY 10.4); cakra-yukta is literal 'joined/fitted with a wheel' and its exact sense (e.g. a wheel jammed) is not certain. The word 'chinna' at the start is printed as such (cch- sandhi not shown).

words.gloss: in injury to a human being

hindi: अन्यथा मनुष्य प्राणी की हिंसा में कहे अनुसार दण्ड लगाए।
english: Otherwise, in injury to a human being, [one] should impose the punishment as stated.
notes: abhyāvahet is literally 'should bring (upon)'; the subject (the king / the judge) is not named. 'As stated' refers to the punishments for injury given earlier (not in this chunk).

words.gloss: in the killing of a non-human creature

hindi: मनुष्य से भिन्न प्राणी के वध में और प्राणी का दान।
english: In the killing of a non-human creature, the giving of a creature as well.
notes: Predicate omitted; 'and' links with the punishment of the previous unit. The giver and receiver are not stated.

words.gloss: one who has attained legal capacity

hindi: चालक के बालक होने पर वाहन में स्थित स्वामी दण्ड के योग्य है; स्वामी न होने पर वाहन में स्थित; अथवा व्यवहार की क्षमता को प्राप्त चालक।
english: When the driver is a child, the owner who is in the vehicle is to be punished; when there is no owner, the one in the vehicle; or the driver who has attained legal capacity.
notes: asvāmini is read as 'when there is no owner [in the vehicle]'; daṇḍyaḥ is carried over to the second and third clauses. prāpta-vyavahāra is literally 'who has reached legal business/proceedings', understood as having attained legal capacity (majority).

hindi: बालक से अधिष्ठित अथवा पुरुष-रहित वाहन को राजा ले ले।
english: The king should take a vehicle occupied by a child or without a man.
notes: hṛ 'take' is kept literal (take away / confiscate is the likely sense).

words.gloss: is to be made to reach

hindi: कृत्य और अभिचार से जो दूसरे को प्राप्त कराए, वही उसे प्राप्त कराया जाए।
english: By kṛtya and abhicāra (sorcery and hostile rites), whatever one makes another undergo, that [he himself] is to be made to undergo.
notes: The e-text joins yat.param and tad.āpādayitavyaḥ with the compound mark, but they are read as separate words (relative 'what' + 'another'; 'that' + gerundive). āpādayet takes two accusatives (another, what). kṛtya = sorcery; abhicāra = hostile rite (not the kṛtya-pakṣa of 12.3). The 'he himself' is supplied by the passive gerundive and bracketed.

hindi: भले ही पत्नी अथवा कन्या न चाहती हो, पत्नी की इच्छा करने वाले का तथा पति के प्रति पत्नी का वशीकरण करना।
english: Granted: the making of winning-over (saṃvadana) — where a wife or maiden is unwilling — [by] one who seeks a wife, or [by] a wife towards a husband.
notes: Obscure; read after unit 27 as an exception for love-winning rites (cf. sāṃvadanikī oṣadhī in GLOSSARY 12.2). kāmam is taken as concessive 'granted' (permitted); the phrase is a noun phrase with no verb, and the grammar of dārārthinaḥ (gen.), bhartari (loc.) and bhāryāyā (gen.) is uncertain. The sense 'permitted' is inferred and bracketing is limited to the supplied 'by'. 'Making of winning-over' is a literal rendering of saṃvadana-karaṇa.

hindi: अन्य प्रकार से की गई हिंसा में मध्यम साहस-दण्ड।
english: In injury done otherwise, the middle fine for rashness.
notes: anyathā-hiṃsā: 'harm done in another way' (than the one just allowed in unit 28).

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. adhi-√car

words.gloss: cutting off of the three liṅgas

hindi: माता और पिता की बहन, मामी, आचार्य की पत्नी, पुत्रवधू, पुत्री अथवा बहन के साथ समागम करने वाले का तीन लिंगों का छेदन और वध।
english: For one who has intercourse with the sister of [his] mother or father, a maternal uncle's wife, a teacher's wife, a daughter-in-law, a daughter or a sister: the cutting off of the three liṅgas, and killing.
notes: adhi-√car is literally 'to go over to / approach' (euphemism for intercourse), as gamana in later units. 'sister of mother and father' = the sister of either parent (dvandva mātā-pitroḥ). tri-liṅga is literal 'three liṅgas (marks/organs)'; probably the male organ and two testicles but not stated. vadha = killing / death. 'his' is bracketed.

words.gloss: enjoyed by a slave, servant or pledged person

hindi: इच्छा रखने वाली स्त्री वही पाए; और दास, परिचारक या आहितक से भोगी गई।
english: A willing woman should receive that very [penalty]; and one enjoyed by a slave, servant or pledged person (āhitaka).
notes: 'penalty' is supplied from unit 30 (the punishment of the woman as for the man). Predicate for the second part is omitted ('and [she] who was enjoyed by…'), so left open. āhitaka is kept as a technical term: literally 'one deposited/pledged' (a person given as a pledge). The meaning of 'bhuktā' = sexually enjoyed.

words.gloss: in the case of a Brahmin woman

hindi: अरक्षित ब्राह्मणी के प्रसंग में क्षत्रिय का सर्वोच्च; वैश्य का सारा धन; शूद्र चटाई की आग से जलाया जाए।
english: In the case of an unguarded Brahmin woman: of a Kshatriya, the highest [fine]; of a Vaishya, all [his] property; a Shudra should be burnt with a fire of mats.
notes: The offence is not stated (intercourse is understood from unit 30); the nouns 'fine' and 'his' are supplied. kaṭa = mat (of reeds or straw). Compare unit 1: the three grades by varṇa.

words.gloss: in intercourse with the king's wife

hindi: सब स्थानों पर राजा की पत्नी से समागम में कुम्भी-पाक।
english: In all cases of intercourse with the king's wife, the kumbhī-pāka (literally 'cooking in a pot').
notes: kumbhī kept untranslated as a technical term (cf. GLOSSARY 13.4); pāka = cooking. gamana literal 'going to'. The punishment is named but its nature is not described here.

words.gloss: in intercourse with a śvapāka woman
one marked with the sign of a headless trunk

hindi: श्वपाकी से समागम में कबन्ध का चिह्न बनवाया हुआ दूसरे देश जाए; अथवा शूद्र श्वपाकत्व को जाए।
english: In intercourse with a śvapāka woman, [the man], marked with the sign of a headless trunk (kabandha), should go to another country; or a Shudra [should go to] the state of a śvapāka.
notes: śvapāka is literally 'dog-cooker' (a low outcaste group); kept as a name. The man in the first clause is not named; 'gacchet' is carried over to the second clause in brackets. kabandha = headless trunk; aṅka = mark/brand. Whether 'should go' means exile or becoming an outcaste is as the Sanskrit; kept literal.

words.gloss: in intercourse with an Arya woman
cutting off of ears and nose

hindi: श्वपाक का आर्या से समागम होने पर वध; स्त्री के कान और नाक का काटना।
english: For a śvapāka's intercourse with an Arya woman, killing; for the woman, the cutting off of ears and nose.
notes: āryā = a noble/respectable (Arya) woman; kept as Arya. vadha = killing.

words.gloss: in intercourse with a female renunciant

hindi: प्रव्रजिता से समागम में चौबीस पण का दण्ड।
english: For intercourse with a female renunciant (pravrajitā), a fine of twenty-four paṇas.
notes: pravrajitā = a woman who has 'gone forth' (renunciant).

hindi: इच्छा रखने वाली स्त्री वही पाए।
english: A willing woman should receive that very [penalty].
notes: Same as the first half of unit 31; 'penalty' supplied from unit 36.

hindi: रूपाजीवा के बलपूर्वक उपभोग में बारह पण का दण्ड।
english: For the forcible enjoyment of a courtesan, a fine of twelve paṇas.
notes: prasahya is an absolutive used as 'by force'; upabhoga = enjoyment (sexual).

words.gram: m. gen. pl. pres. part. adhi-√car

hindi: एक के साथ समागम करने वाले बहुतों का अलग-अलग चौबीस पण का दण्ड।
english: For many who have intercourse with one [woman], a fine of twenty-four paṇas separately.
notes: 'woman' is bracketed (ekām is feminine). adhicarat as in unit 30.

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. adhi-√mih

hindi: स्त्री के साथ अयोनि में समागम करने वाले को प्रथम साहस-दण्ड; और पुरुष पर मूत्र करने वाले को।
english: For one who has intercourse with a woman in a non-yoni (ayoni), the first fine for rashness; and for one who urinates upon a man.
notes: ayoni = 'not the yoni' (literal). adhi-√mih: 'urinate upon' (mih can also mean emit semen); the second clause leaves the fine implied (the same first grade).

hindi: पशु-योनियों में मैथुन करने पर, अपने वश में न रहने वाले का, बारह पण; और देव-प्रतिमाओं के साथ समागम में दुगुना माना गया है।
english: For copulation with animals (tiryag-yoni, 'animal wombs'), of one not self-possessed, twelve paṇas; and for intercourse with images of deities, double is held.
notes: tiryag-yoni = animals (literally 'sideways-born'). anātmanaḥ is read 'of one not self-possessed' (anātman; cf. GLOSSARY ātmavān); the sense (lacking self-control / unnatural) is uncertain. 'fine' is not in the Sanskrit; paṇas imply it. smṛta = 'remembered/held' (traditional).

hindi: दण्ड के अयोग्य को दण्ड देने पर राजा का दण्ड तीस गुना है; जल में वरुण को दिया जाना चाहिए, उसके बाद ब्राह्मणों को।
english: For punishing one who is not to be punished, the king's fine is thirtyfold, to be given in the water to Varuna, and thereafter to Brahmins.
notes: Thirtyfold of what (the penalty wrongly imposed) is implied, not stated. 'in water' is read with pradātavyaḥ. tataḥ param = 'thereafter'.

words.gloss: born of wrong conduct in punishment

words.gram: m. gen. pl. pres. part. vi-ā-√car

hindi: उससे राजा का दण्ड में अनुचित आचरण से उत्पन्न वह पाप शुद्ध हो जाता है; क्योंकि मनुष्यों में मिथ्या आचरण करने वाले राजाओं का वरुण शास्ता है।
english: By that, the king's sin born of wrong conduct in punishment is purified; for Varuna is the chastiser of kings who act wrongly among men.
notes: śāstṛ means ruler/instructor/punisher; 'chastiser' is chosen. apacāra = wrong conduct, transgression. 'wrongly acting among men' (nṛṣu) is taken with vyācaratām.
